1.explanation:
• gather/gatherers/offline-test.js: Implements the offline pass, toggling network conditions to offline and should trigger the fallback UI.
• gather/gatherers/start-url-test.js: Attempts to fetch the start URL during the offline pass; if it fails, it collects the offline error that powers the fallback.
• gather/gatherers/service-worker-test.js: Verifies service-worker interception logic, essential for understanding why requests aren’t served from SW cache.
• audits/offline-start-url-test.js: The audit that reports whether the start URL loads offline; central to the observed failure.
• audits/service-worker-test.js: Checks SW registration and scope; if mis-configured, network requests won’t be intercepted offline.
• runner-test.js: Orchestrates gather–audit passes (including switching to offline), showing how offline-pass flow is implemented and where it may break.
1.bug_scenario: The provided screenshot shows Lighthouse’s offline fallback UI (“⚠️ You are offline” heading plus explanatory paragraph) which should appear when the start URL is unavailable offline. However, in the bug reproduction, Lighthouse’s “offline pass” is actually loading the site’s desktop version and all network requests report neither `fromServiceWorker` nor `fromDiskCache`. The offline fallback UI never appears even though the test is running completely offline. Key UI elements involved are the warning icon, heading text (“You are offline”), the explanatory message, and the blank background where offline content should be rendered.
